label: lem:continuous_at_interior
title: Continuity at interior points
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, and let $x \in (\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x$ within $\mathrm{Ioi}\; x$ (i.e.\ \texttt{ContinuousWithinAt f (Ioi x) x}). This follows from the fact that continuity on a set implies continuity at any interior point, restricted to any subset.
proof: Since $x$ is in the interior of $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, continuity on the closed interval implies continuity at $x$. Restricting to $\mathrm{Ioi}\; x$ preserves this, since $\mathrm{Ioi}\; x \subseteq [\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ near $x$.
